title: ticfac Phase 2: the Herdr executor
description: SPEC §12 Phase 2. Herdr executor behind the same four operations; move execution-oriented Herdr process/fleet helpers out of internal/herd/**; support a range of Herdr protocol versions (hard floor, warn version, no upper bound); retain tracker-domain configuration and the question relay in ticks; move internal/factory/** and Factory commands to the ticfac CLI without hidden tk dispatch shims; replace every ticks internal Go import with tk --json, Git or a pinned schema.
notes:
2026-09-02 13:29 - Overlap: 'replace every ticks internal Go import' was largely done by a4n Phase 5a (g0b; closeout q71 still open). This phase verifies and finishes it rather than redoing it.
2026-09-02 16:52 - REQUIRED GATE TESTS (Peter, 2026-09-02): two recurring failures of the current tk herd orchestration must be conformance tests of the Herdr executor, not guidance.
(a) Finished-worker detection. The orchestrator repeatedly failed to notice settled workers. Tests: inspect() reports completed from DURABLE evidence (commits beyond base + RESULT on the branch), never from pane lifecycle state; a worker that settles while no wait is open is detected by the next inspect (no lost-event race); a worker that goes idle with work parked in harness background tasks is reported settled-but-incomplete, not done; a wait that was killed and re-issued sees the already-settled worker immediately; an agent herdr no longer lists is reported exited and then settled from durable evidence (Appendix A #5, #8). Include a live test against a real herdr (like scripts/verify-herd-helper.sh) plus the fake-harness sequences.
(b) Orphaned worker workspaces. Runs left worker workspaces/worktrees behind. Tests: cleanup after a completed job leaves ZERO run-created workspaces in herdr workspace list (including the implicitly opened source-checkout workspace); a crashed orchestrator's next reconcile lists every workspace it created and classifies each (live/dead-resumable/dead-with-work/stale) with none unaccounted; workspace removal order (linked worktrees before the checkout workspace) is enforced; a refused cleanup (blocked/unmerged) is reported, never silently skipped; focus is restored to the pre-run workspace. Identity for both: (repo key, run id, tick, attempt), never agent name alone (cf. legacy 5jo).
acceptance_criteria: Gate: the operator runs a real ticks epic for actual work through ticfac run-epic on Herdr instead of the tk herd skill ritual, and it completes.
closed_reason: ticfac Phase 2 complete in the ticfac repository (epic av8, 81 commits, gate green). The herdr executor exists behind the unchanged five-operation seam, a real epic ran end to end through ticfac run-epic on herdr, the herdr protocol and server version are in the pinned provenance, and ticfac has NO Go dependency on ticks — every crossing is tk --json, git, or a pinned schema. Robustness to protocol updates achieved: a supported range rather than a pin, rename-loud decoding, a vocabulary diffed against the live binary, and a collect path that makes zero herdr calls so a substrate failure can never become a verdict. NOT done and carried into ticfac Phase 3 (epic 9pd): nothing has been REMOVED from this repository — internal/herd's execution packages and internal/factory still live here as a second implementation — because a tick whose work is in another repo cannot be dispatched. Details in .tick/logs/herd/av8/RETRO.md in ticfac.
